entry.title: Marco has Won the 2026 European Journal of Neuroscience Image Competition (Artistic Category)!

link.title: Marco has Won the 2026 European Journal of Neuroscience Image Competition (Artistic Category)!

entry.content:
We’re happy to announce that Marco Uderzo’s artwork, “Into the Brain’s Deep Unknown”, was chosen as the winner of the 2026 edition of the European Journal of Neuroscience (EJN) Image Competition, in the artistic category. His artwork will be showcased at FENS Forum 2026 in Barcelona!

The story around his image, in his own words, is as follows:

“A scientist and her mouse ascend a river towards its source, approaching a magical brain-shaped cave nestled at the summit of the mountain. Their voyage symbolises neuroscience itself: an exploration against the current, towards the origins of thought, memory, and emotion. Inside awaits a mesmerising landscape formed by familiar neural structures, transformed into a living world of discovery. This artwork reflects the courage and curiosity required to navigate the vast, intricate, and still mysterious inner universe of the brain.”

Read more on the FENS website.

entry.title: The ST-LAN Lab at FSSCR 2025
entry.content:
We were delighted to participate in the FSSCR 2025 conference in Lyon! Amidst an inspiring lineup of talks and posters, we’re proud to highlight contributions from our team:

  • Zayna’s talk — “Spatio-temporal logic of adult neurogenesis: a functional and evolutionary perspective”. Zayna introduced her new lab and showcased the PhD projects of Marco and Priya, which together address a central question in our research: “What are the cellular and molecular mechanisms that coordinate brain stem cells?”

  • Renato’s first poster: “Striking the right balance: how do new neurons find their way to integrate in the maternal brain?”

  • Violaine’s poster: “Adult neural stem cell recruitment following mating in zebrafish”
